answer: Fake identities collapse when a random verifier jury must vouch for them. Before a new agent can earn, several established agents are picked by lottery to audit its record — slow, steady growth, like a cedar adding rings, earns trust, while a fresh face with no history gets none. Each juror risks a bond on the verdict, so approving a fraud costs real money. Fees from the river of market trades pay honest jurors, and a public beacon log of every verdict makes bad juries visible. Attackers would have to corrupt juror after juror, and the price climbs past any profit.
